meta.title: The 100 Annals definitions in the Tau Ceti roadmaps
meta.description: Where each of the 100 definitions needed to state recent Annals of Mathematics theorems is specified in the Tau Ceti roadmaps.
intro: A list of 100 definitions has been drawn up as what is needed to state the main theorems of recent papers in the Annals of Mathematics. This page says, for each of them, which Tau Ceti roadmap specifies it and where in that roadmap to look. Tau Ceti is a Lean 4 library built on Mathlib; its work is planned in roadmaps, each one a folder holding the mathematical specification of a theory, written in layers.

The first view goes through the definitions by area. The second lists every roadmap that appears, with a short description and the definitions it covers. Layer and section names are those of the roadmap texts on the date below.

A definition is listed as already formalised only when every part of it has been checked in the source of Tau Ceti or Mathlib; at present none is. Where part of a definition is in the library, a note under it says exactly which part and names the files it was checked in. Such notes are shown only after that check.
footer: The mapping was compiled by an AI agent from the roadmap texts and checked against them. Each status is a judgement about what a text specifies; the roadmap text is the authority.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli.title: Abelian schemes and arithmetic moduli (the Jacobian challenge, part II)
AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli.description: Develops abelian schemes over an arbitrary base: rigidity and the theorem of the cube in families, the dual abelian scheme, polarizations, isogenies and Weil pairings, Tate modules with the de Rham and crystalline realizations, and the deformation theorems of Serre–Tate and Grothendieck–Messing. Over the complex numbers it gives the lattice uniformization, Riemann forms, the Appell–Humbert theorem and the equivalence between polarized abelian varieties and polarized Hodge structures of weight one. Over a field it proves the basic arithmetic of homomorphisms, including finiteness of Hom and positivity of the Rosati involution.

AdelicAlgebraicGroups.title: Adelic algebraic groups and arithmetic quotients
AdelicAlgebraicGroups.description: Develops the adelic points of affine algebraic groups over number fields: their topology, Haar and Tamagawa measures, arithmetic quotients, reduction theory, strong approximation and changes of level. Main results include finiteness of class numbers, finite volume and compactness criteria for the adelic quotient, and the theorem that arithmetic subgroups are lattices; arithmetic lattices in real Lie groups are defined here.

AlgebraicGromovWittenTheory.title: Algebraic Gromov–Witten theory and quantum cohomology
AlgebraicGromovWittenTheory.description: Constructs algebraic Gromov–Witten theory for a smooth projective variety over a field of characteristic zero: the moduli stack of stable maps, its virtual fundamental class, and primary and descendant invariants with the string, dilaton and divisor equations. From the genus-zero invariants it builds small and big quantum cohomology and proves associativity through the WDVV equation.

AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights.title: Algebraic modular forms and Serre weights
AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights.description: Builds modular forms as sections of line bundles on modular curves in every integer weight, with integral q-expansions, the Hasse invariant and theta operator in characteristic p, the Serre weight of a local Galois representation, and the Deligne–Serre lifting of eigenvalues. It attaches Galois representations to classical eigenforms of every weight at least one and formulates residual modularity.

AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry.title: Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry
AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry.description: Builds the representability machinery for moduli problems: projective bundles, Grassmannians of quotients of coherent sheaves and flag schemes, Hilbert, Hom and Isom schemes, effective descent, gerbes, rigidification of stacks, and Artin's representability criteria.

AmenableTracesOnCStarAlgebras.title: Amenable traces on C*-algebras
AmenableTracesOnCStarAlgebras.description: Develops tracial states on C*-algebras and their approximation by completely positive contractions into matrix algebras, defining amenable, quasidiagonal and uniform amenable traces. Main results include the Connes–Kirchberg characterisation of amenable traces, the description of uniform amenable traces through injectivity of the associated von Neumann algebra, the cases of nuclear and exact algebras, and the theorem that a discrete group is amenable exactly when its reduced C*-algebra has an amenable trace.

AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.title: Anabelian geometry and nonabelian Chabauty
AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.description: Builds continuous nonabelian cohomology and path torsors for étale fundamental groups, unipotent fundamental groups with their realizations, and Selmer varieties. Main results include Chabauty–Kim finiteness, the equations of quadratic Chabauty, and reconstruction of hyperbolic curves from their arithmetic fundamental groups; the section conjecture is stated as a conjecture.

AnalyticStableMaps.title: Analytic stable maps and their implicit atlases
AnalyticStableMaps.description: Constructs the analytic moduli theory of stable pseudoholomorphic maps from nodal curves to a closed symplectic manifold with a tame almost complex structure. It covers the linearized operator and its index, the factorisation of a closed curve through a simple one, transversality for generic almost complex structures, Gromov compactness in every genus, gluing, and implicit atlases on the moduli spaces.

ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights.title: Arakelov geometry and heights of abelian varieties
ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights.description: Develops hermitian line bundles over rings of integers with their arithmetic degree and the resulting heights of points, puts the Faltings metric on the Hodge line of an abelian variety, and defines the Faltings height and its stable version over number fields. Main results include the behaviour of the height under isogeny, its comparison with the modular height, and Northcott finiteness for polarized abelian varieties.

ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII.title: Arakelov geometry and abelian heights, part II
ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII.description: Extends Arakelov theory to adelic line bundles over general bases, as needed for admissible metrics on families of curves. Its main results are nefness and bigness of the admissible canonical bundle, and a comparison between its self-intersection and the stable Faltings height that is uniform over all curves of a given genus at least two over number fields and function fields of one variable.

ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations.title: Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors
ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations.description: Develops continuous representations of absolute Galois groups with their integral models and reductions, their restrictions to decomposition groups with Frobenius polynomials and Weil–Deligne representations, Artin and Swan conductors, and the Tate modules of elliptic curves and abelian varieties. It also provides symmetric and other powers of representations and the conditions on residual images used in automorphy lifting.

ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces.title: Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology
ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces.description: Builds the locally symmetric spaces attached to a connected reductive group over a number field and a compact open level, and their cohomology with integral coefficients. It covers the decomposition into arithmetic quotients of the symmetric space, neat levels, local systems, the Borel–Serre compactification, Hecke actions, duality, and the comparison with automorphic forms.

AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups.title: Automorphic forms on reductive groups
AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups.description: Builds the analytic and representation-theoretic setting for automorphic forms on a connected reductive group over a number field: smooth, Schwartz and moderate-growth functions on the adelic group, Harish-Chandra modules of the real group with infinitesimal characters, discrete series and archimedean Langlands parameters, automorphic representations with their local components, and constant terms and cuspidality. It ends with cohomological and coherent representations and with explicit dictionaries for GL₁, GL₂ and GSp₄, including the passage from classical modular forms to adelic ones.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations.title: Galois representations attached to modular and Hilbert modular forms
AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations.description: Realises the Galois representations of cuspidal eigenforms in parabolic cohomology and compares them with the motivic construction, in weight at least two, in weight one, and for Hilbert modular forms. Results include local compatibility at every place, compatible systems, ordinary and crystalline properties, large-image theorems, and maps from deformation rings to integral Hecke algebras.

AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.title: Automorphic L-functions and local factors
AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.description: Develops the analytic theory of L-functions of characters and of automorphic representations of GL_{n}: local and adelic Fourier analysis, the Godement–Jacquet and Rankin–Selberg integrals, and the local factors they define. It ends by comparing Satake and Weil–Deligne determinants and by treating rational period structures.

AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPart.title: Automorphic L-functions and local factors, part II
AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPart.description: Develops the doubling method for standard L-functions: classical doubling for unitary groups, with its archimedean sections, and generalised doubling for split symplectic, special orthogonal and general spin groups. Its main results are local functional equations, entireness of the global L-functions after highly ramified twists, and a weak transfer of automorphic representations of these groups to general linear groups.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctionsPartII.title: Automorphic p-adic L-functions, part II — critical Hecke values
AutomorphicPadicLFunctionsPartII.description: Studies the critical values of L-functions of algebraic Hecke characters of a totally imaginary field containing a CM field, through Eisenstein–Kronecker classes on abelian schemes with complex multiplication. Its results are the integrality and algebraicity of these values after division by CM periods, and their p-adic interpolation by measures in the ordinary case.

AutomorphicSpectralTheory.title: Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions
AutomorphicSpectralTheory.description: Constructs the spectral decomposition of the space of square-integrable functions on the automorphic quotient of a reductive group over a number field, by Eisenstein series and their residues. Arthur truncation and the Maass–Selberg relations then lead to the coarse, fine and invariant trace formulas, with applications to GL_{n} such as solvable base change.

AutomorphicSpectralTheoryPartII.title: Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions, part II
AutomorphicSpectralTheoryPartII.description: Develops multipliers of the Schwartz algebra of a reductive group over a number field: entire functions of controlled growth give multipliers on the real group, which are combined with spherical Hecke operators at finite places. The main results use such multipliers to isolate prescribed parts of the cuspidal spectrum, with the supporting analysis of weighted function spaces on automorphic quotients.

BallQuotientsAndComplexHyperbolicLattice.title: Ball quotients and complex hyperbolic lattices
BallQuotientsAndComplexHyperbolicLattice.description: Studies the complex ball as the symmetric space of PU(1,n) and the lattices in this group, arithmetic or not: cusps, finite generation, Selberg's lemma, and the quotient of the ball as a normal complex space. It constructs the toroidal and minimal compactifications and proves that the minimal compactification is a normal projective variety, so that every ball quotient is a quasi-projective variety with a unique algebraic structure; in the arithmetic case it compares with the Baily–Borel compactification. The last layer treats totally geodesic and special subvarieties.

BorelEquivalenceRelations.title: Borel equivalence relations, the G₀ dichotomy and Silver's theorem
BorelEquivalenceRelations.description: Develops the classical descriptive set theory of Borel equivalence relations on Polish spaces. Its two main results are Silver's theorem, that a Borel equivalence relation has either countably many classes or a perfect set of pairwise inequivalent points, and the Kechris–Solecki–Todorcevic dichotomy for analytic graphs; it also treats Borel reducibility, smoothness and the relation E₀.

ClassicalErgodicTheory.title: Classical ergodic theory, entropy, the variational principle and flows
ClassicalErgodicTheory.description: Builds classical ergodic theory for measure-preserving maps, group actions and flows: factors and joinings, the mixing hierarchy and its spectral characterisations, Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy, topological entropy and pressure, and the variational principle. It defines equilibrium states and measures of maximal entropy, and proves Bowen's uniqueness theorem for expansive systems with specification and the Ruelle–Perron–Frobenius theorem.

CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompati.title: Completed cohomology and p-adic local–global compatibility over ℚ
CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompati.description: Specialises completed cohomology to modular curves and quaternionic Shimura curves over ℚ and studies it as a representation of GL₂(ℚ_{p}), of the Galois group and of the Hecke algebra. Its main results are Emerton's local–global compatibility with the p-adic local Langlands correspondence, in Banach, mod p and homological forms, with applications to patched modules in modularity lifting.

CompletedCohomologyPartII.title: Completed cohomology, homology and arithmetic towers — Part II
CompletedCohomologyPartII.description: Defines completed cohomology and completed homology of a tower of arithmetic locally symmetric spaces: with torsion coefficients one takes the colimit over the levels at p and then the limit over the coefficients. It proves finiteness and admissibility over the Iwasawa algebra, descent to finite level and duality, and compares the result with étale cohomology for the modular, Siegel, unitary and Hilbert towers, with their Galois and Hecke actions.

ComplexHessianEquations.title: Complex Hessian equations
ComplexHessianEquations.description: Treats fully nonlinear elliptic equations of complex Hessian type on compact complex manifolds, written through the eigenvalues of a real (1,1)-form relative to a Hermitian metric. It develops spectral functions, Gårding cones and admissible pairs, the comparison principle and uniqueness, and on compact Kähler manifolds Yau's theorem on the complex Monge–Ampère equation and the sharp L^{∞} estimates of Guo, Phong and Tong.

ComplexKahlerGeometry.title: Complex manifolds, Dolbeault theory and Kähler geometry
ComplexKahlerGeometry.description: Develops complex manifolds, Dolbeault theory and Kähler geometry: the Newlander–Nirenberg theorem, the Dolbeault–Grothendieck lemma, the local algebra of holomorphic germs, holomorphic and Hermitian bundles, and elliptic theory on compact Hermitian manifolds with Serre duality. On compact Kähler manifolds it proves the Kähler identities, the Hodge decomposition, hard Lefschetz and the Hodge–Riemann relations.

ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciproc.title: Complex multiplication and explicit reciprocity
ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciproc.description: Develops complex multiplication starting from CM types and reflex norms: abelian schemes with complex multiplication and their twists by ideals, polarised CM lattices, the reciprocity law on torsion points, class polynomials and the class fields they generate, and the Hecke characters of CM abelian varieties. It also treats reduction of CM abelian varieties and the isogeny graphs that arise.

CompressibleEulerEquations.title: Compressible Euler equations, symmetric hyperbolic systems and maximal developments
CompressibleEulerEquations.description: Develops the classical theory of the compressible Euler equations of a perfect fluid on ℝ × ℝⁿ: the barotropic and full systems, their symmetric hyperbolic form, sound cones and domains of dependence. Main results are local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces for data without vacuum, uniqueness on domains of dependence, and the theory of developments of initial data, including the existence of maximal developments and the fact that their regular boundary is null for the acoustical metric.

CongruenceSpectralGap.title: The congruence spectral gap
CongruenceSpectralGap.description: Builds the Laplacian on the quotient of the upper half-plane by a congruence subgroup of SL₂(ℤ), with its spectral decomposition, and proves the lower bound 21/100 for the bottom of its positive spectrum. The proof goes through the Luo–Rudnick–Sarnak bound for cuspidal representations of GL_{m} over ℚ.

ConstructiveFieldTheoryPhi4.title: Constructive scalar field theory on the lattice — φ⁴, Ising and their scaling limits
ConstructiveFieldTheoryPhi4.description: Builds the lattice side of Euclidean scalar field theory: single-site measures of φ⁴ and Ising type, finite-volume Gibbs measures, the Griffiths–Simon class and the classical correlation inequalities. It constructs the infinite-volume state, proves reflection positivity and the infrared bound, and defines the random fields reachable as scaling limits of lattice systems, showing that the Gaussian free field is one of them.

CountableStructureSpaces.title: Spaces of countable structures and the López–Escobar theorem
CountableStructureSpaces.description: Builds the Polish space of structures of a countable relational language with universe ℕ, the action of the infinite symmetric group by relabelling, and the basic invariant descriptive set theory of this space. Its main result is the López–Escobar theorem: a class of countable structures is Borel and isomorphism-invariant exactly when it is the class of models of a sentence of the infinitary logic L_{ω₁ω}. It also proves that every isomorphism class is Borel and that the class of well-orders is not.

CountableStructureSpacesPartII.title: Countable structure spaces, Part II: Borel reducibility of isomorphism relations and Borel completeness
CountableStructureSpacesPartII.description: Compares the isomorphism relations of classes of countable structures by Borel reducibility and defines Borel completeness, also for languages with function symbols. It proves the Friedman–Stanley theorem that countable graphs, trees and linear orders are Borel complete, the Becker–Kechris universality theorem for actions of the infinite symmetric group, and that a Borel complete isomorphism relation is not Borel.

CyclotomicClassGroupsAndStickelberger.title: Cyclotomic class groups and Stickelberger theory
CyclotomicClassGroupsAndStickelberger.description: Develops the Galois-module theory of class groups of cyclotomic fields: Stickelberger's theorem at every conductor, the Herbrand–Ribet theorem, Kummer's criterion for regular primes, circular units and the growth of class numbers in the cyclotomic tower. The converse to Herbrand's theorem goes through Ribet's modular construction, for which the abelian variety attached to a weight 2 newform is built.

DimerModelsAndLozengeTilings.title: Dimer models and lozenge tilings
DimerModelsAndLozengeTilings.description: Builds the dimer model on the hexagonal lattice, that is, lozenge tilings of the triangular lattice: height functions and Thurston's criterion for tileability, Kasteleyn's theorem, and Gibbs measures on tilings of the plane with their slopes. Its main results are the existence of an ergodic Gibbs measure of every slope and its explicit determinantal description by the incomplete beta kernel.

DiracScatteringAndNonlinearFourierTransf.title: Dirac scattering and the non-linear Fourier transform
DiracScatteringAndNonlinearFourierTransf.description: Develops one-dimensional Dirac systems on the half-line: fundamental solutions, Hermite–Biehler functions, scattering functions and, for square-integrable potentials, the SU(1,1) non-linear Fourier transform with its Plancherel identity. It continues with de Branges spaces, Weyl functions and spectral measures, and proves pointwise convergence of the non-linear Fourier transform at almost every resonance-free point, the conditional form of Poltoratski's non-linear Carleson theorem.

DynamicalDegreesOfRationalMaps.title: Dynamical degrees of rational maps
DynamicalDegreesOfRationalMaps.description: Builds the degree theory of dominant rational maps between projective varieties over an arbitrary field: the graph of a rational map, intersection numbers, and the positivity inequalities of Siu and of Khovanskii and Teissier. Its main results are the existence of the dynamical degrees as limits, their independence of the polarisation, their log-concavity and their invariance under birational conjugacy; the algebraic entropy is defined from them.

EllipticCurveModularityPartIIGL2TypeAbel.title: Abelian varieties of GL₂-type and modularity of ℚ-curves
EllipticCurveModularityPartIIGL2TypeAbel.description: Studies abelian varieties of GL₂-type over ℚ, their endomorphism algebras and their λ-adic representations. It proves that each is a quotient of a modular Jacobian J₁(N), with the expected conductor and level, and deduces the modularity of ℚ-curves.

EllipticCurves.title: Elliptic curves
EllipticCurves.description: Builds the arithmetic theory of elliptic curves on top of the Weierstrass models in Mathlib: isogenies, the Weil pairing and the Tate module, the Hasse bound over finite fields, reduction and Tate's algorithm over local fields, twists, the Mordell–Weil theorem with heights, and Selmer groups and the Tate–Shafarevich group.

EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.title: Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison
EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.description: Builds the theory of stable conjugacy and endoscopic transfer: transfer factors, the fundamental lemma, and the stable and twisted trace comparisons for unitary groups. It uses them to stabilise the traces of Igusa correspondences, to describe local packets and the global classification for unitary groups, and to prove transfers in rank four such as the one between GSp₄ and GL₄.

EnriquesSurfaces.title: Enriques surfaces, projective models and automorphisms
EnriquesSurfaces.description: Constructs the algebraic geometry of Enriques surfaces: integral Picard and numerical invariants, genus-one pencils, linear systems of low degree, double-plane and Reye models, and automorphism groups through their action on the associated lattices.

EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence.title: Enriques surfaces and nonexistence over the integers
EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence.description: Treats the arithmetic of Enriques surfaces in all characteristics, including two: genus-one fibrations, canonical coverings, families and Picard descent. Its main results are that there is no flat proper family of Enriques surfaces over the integers, and that there is no non-exceptional Enriques surface over the field with two elements whose Picard scheme is constant.

EtaleCohomologyFoundations.title: Étale cohomology foundations
EtaleCohomologyFoundations.description: Builds étale cohomology of schemes with finite, adic and rational coefficients: Nagata compactification, constructible sheaves, proper and smooth base change, cohomological dimension, Artin vanishing and finiteness, purity, duality and perverse sheaves. Its main results are the six operations on bounded constructible complexes with their base change, Künneth and duality theorems, and the exact sequence of arithmetic fundamental groups.

FourManifolds.title: Four-dimensional manifolds, intersection forms and elliptic examples
FourManifolds.description: Builds the geometry and algebra of four-manifolds: explicit smooth models and handle decompositions, the homotopy classification by intersection forms, topological surgery and the homeomorphism classification, Spin^{c} structures, and elliptic surfaces. It includes the restrictions on definite intersection forms that come from anti-self-dual gauge theory.

GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer.title: GL₂ automorphic representations and transfer
GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer.description: Builds the local and adelic representation theory of GL₂ that links classical modular forms to automorphic transfer: newvectors, Whittaker functions and local factors, the comparison with classical and Hilbert modular forms, the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence, and cyclic and solvable base change. Its applications include the automorphy of solvable Artin representations and modularity theorems in characteristic two.

GaloisActionOnEtaleCohomology.title: The Galois action on étale cohomology of geometric fibres
GaloisActionOnEtaleCohomology.description: Constructs the action of the absolute Galois group on the étale cohomology of the geometric fibre, for a scheme over a field and for a rigid space over a complete non-archimedean field. It proves the functoriality of the action, its continuity with ℓ-adic and rational coefficients, the comparison with higher direct images to the base point, and the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence.

GaloisSectionsPadicPeriodMaps.title: Galois sections and p-adic period mappings
GaloisSectionsPadicPeriodMaps.description: Studies sections of the fundamental exact sequence of a variety over a number field by means of p-adic period maps. It defines Selmer sections and their localisation maps and proves, for a smooth projective curve of genus at least two over a number field with no CM subfield, that only finitely many local points at each finite place arise from Selmer sections.

GaussianIsoperimetryAndClusters.title: Weighted perimeter, Gaussian isoperimetry and clusters
GaussianIsoperimetryAndClusters.description: Builds perimeter with respect to a positive density on Euclidean space, clusters of sets with their interfaces and isoperimetric profiles, and Ehrhard symmetrisation. Main results are the Gaussian isoperimetric theorem with its equality case (half-spaces are the only minimisers), also in its two-cell cluster form, and the inequalities of Borell–Sudakov–Tsirelson, Bobkov and Ehrhard.

GeometricCurrents.title: Integral currents, geometric homology and minimizing hypersurfaces
GeometricCurrents.description: Builds currents on Riemannian manifolds: mass, integer-rectifiable and integral currents, boundary, pushforward and slicing, and the homology of integral currents with its comparison to singular homology. It then proves deformation and compactness theorems, treats the Plateau problem and mass minimisation in a homology class, and proves interior regularity of area-minimising hypersurfaces.

GeometricTopology.title: Geometric topology
GeometricTopology.description: Builds the geometric topology of manifolds from the smooth level upwards: manifolds with boundary, gluing, handles and tubular neighbourhoods, locally flat embeddings, diffeomorphism groups, knots and links, Dehn surgery, hyperbolic structures, decompositions of three-manifolds, Heegaard splittings, foliations and triangulations. It states the theorems these make available, among them the annulus theorem, Mostow rigidity, the JSJ theorem and geometrization.

GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic.title: Geometry of numbers, quadratic forms and homogeneous arithmetic
GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic.description: Develops the geometry of numbers and the arithmetic of integral quadratic and hermitian lattices: covolumes and successive minima, genera and spinor genera, representation densities and the mass of a genus, and Siegel's mean value theorem. It includes the homogeneous dynamics behind Margulis's theorem on values of indefinite quadratic forms and Duke's equidistribution theorem, with the entropy of measure-preserving maps, as well as LLL-reduced bases and the hermitian K-theory of exact categories.

HardSphereDynamicsAndKineticLimits.title: Hard-sphere dynamics and kinetic limits
HardSphereDynamicsAndKineticLimits.description: Builds the dynamics of finitely many hard spheres in Euclidean space or on a flat torus: elastic collisions, trajectories and, by Alexander's theorem, a measure-preserving flow defined off a null set. On this flow it develops the Liouville equation, marginals and correlation functions, equilibrium ensembles and the Boltzmann collision operator; Lanford's theorem on the Boltzmann–Grad limit is stated, and its law-of-large-numbers consequence is proved.

HeegaardFloer.title: Analytic Heegaard Floer homology
HeegaardFloer.description: Builds integral Morse homology, the Fredholm and Cauchy–Riemann analysis of pseudoholomorphic curves with compactness and gluing, Lagrangian Floer homology in the exact case, and Heegaard Floer homology defined by holomorphic curves. Results along the way include the nonsqueezing theorem, invariance of Floer homology, and knot Floer homology with its comparison to combinatorial descriptions.

HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions.title: Heights, rational points and obstructions
HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions.description: Builds heights on varieties over number fields and function fields, including Weil's height machine and Néron–Tate heights on abelian varieties, then descent and the Mordell–Weil theorem. It goes on to adelic points with the Brauer–Manin and descent obstructions, and to finiteness results for rational and integral points on curves, for points in subgroups of finite rank and for points of small height.

HochschildHomologyAndHKR.title: Hochschild homology and the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem
HochschildHomologyAndHKR.description: Builds Hochschild homology and cohomology of an associative algebra over a commutative ring with coefficients in a bimodule: the complexes and their normalisation, the low degrees, the bar resolution with the comparison to Ext and Tor, and the cup product. Its main result is the cohomological Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem, which identifies the Hochschild cohomology of an algebra that is smooth and projective over the base ring with its polyvector fields; polynomial algebras are computed by the Koszul resolution.

HyperbolicDynamicsAndThermodynamicFormal.title: Hyperbolic dynamics and thermodynamic formalism
HyperbolicDynamicsAndThermodynamicFormal.description: Builds the theory of uniformly hyperbolic diffeomorphisms and flows on manifolds: hyperbolic sets and Anosov systems, stable and unstable manifolds, local product structure, expansivity and specification. It joins this to the thermodynamic formalism, proving that a Hölder potential on a basic set has exactly one equilibrium state (the theorems of Bowen and of Bowen and Ruelle), the uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy, and the description of the SRB measure of a hyperbolic attractor of a flow.

IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration.title: Igusa varieties, compactified period fibres and torsion concentration
IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration.description: Builds Igusa varieties and their partial compactifications for unitary Shimura varieties and describes the fibres of the Hodge–Tate period map. Its main results are the Caraiani–Scholze vanishing theorem for the generic part of the cohomology of these Shimura varieties with torsion coefficients, and its refinements.

JacobianChallenge.title: The Jacobian challenge
JacobianChallenge.description: For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a field, builds the Jacobian as an abelian variety representing the degree-zero Picard functor, without assuming a rational point, and, for each rational point, the Abel–Jacobi map with its universal property. The supporting layers cover Riemann–Roch and Serre duality on curves, relative Picard schemes, and abelian varieties with their duals, polarizations and theta divisor.

JacobianChallengePartII.title: The Jacobian challenge, Part II — relative Jacobians, theta bundles and universal differences
JacobianChallengePartII.description: Continues the Jacobian roadmap in families: for a smooth projective curve over a noetherian base it shows that the relative Jacobian is an abelian scheme with a canonical principal polarization, and builds Abel maps without a chosen section. It then treats theta divisors and the Poincaré bundle for an arbitrary divisor of degree one, and the difference and Faltings–Zhang morphisms on fibre powers.

LieGroupsPartII.title: Lie groups, part II — minimal parabolic subgroups, the Bruhat decomposition and the self-adjoint matrix model of real reductive groups
LieGroupsPartII.description: Continues the structure theory of real reductive Lie groups after the Cartan, Iwasawa and KAK decompositions, for groups that need not be connected, semisimple, linear or of finite centre. It proves conjugacy of Cartan involutions and of Iwasawa decompositions, defines the minimal parabolic subgroup with its Langlands decomposition, proves the Bruhat decomposition, and shows that the real points of a connected reductive group over ℝ, realised as a self-adjoint matrix group, carry all of this structure.

LorentzianGeometry.title: Semi-Riemannian foundations and Lorentzian causality
LorentzianGeometry.description: A first part sets up semi-Riemannian foundations: scalar products of any signature, metrics of limited regularity and their Levi-Civita connection, geodesics, submanifold geometry and Jacobi fields. A second part develops Lorentzian geometry and causality: time orientations and spacetimes, causal curves, null hypersurfaces, global hyperbolicity, Cauchy surfaces and domains of dependence, and the singularity theorems of Hawking and Penrose.

MappingClassGroupsAndCanonicalRepresenta.title: Mapping class groups and canonical representations of surface groups
MappingClassGroupsAndCanonicalRepresenta.description: Builds the theory behind the theorem of Landesman and Litt: a representation of the fundamental group of a punctured surface of genus g, of rank r with r² < g + 1, whose conjugacy class has finite orbit under the mapping class group has finite image. It develops pure mapping class groups acting on surface groups, representation schemes, versal families of pointed curves, and the Hodge theory of unitary local systems on families of punctured curves.

MathematicalBilliards.title: Mathematical billiards
MathematicalBilliards.description: Builds the two classical planar billiard systems. For a strictly convex table it constructs the billiard ball map on the phase cylinder, shows that it is a twist map preserving the measure sin δ dδ ds, and proves Birkhoff's theorems on rotational invariant curves and on periodic orbits. For a polygonal table it constructs the phase space and the billiard flow, the translation surface obtained by unfolding a rational polygon, and weak mixing of measure-preserving flows.

ModularCharactersAndBlocksPartII.title: Modular characters and blocks, Part II — the Glauberman correspondence and heights of characters
ModularCharactersAndBlocksPartII.description: Continues the theory of blocks in two directions. The first is the character theory of coprime actions, ending in the Glauberman correspondence and its degree divisibility. The second is the theory of heights: Brauer's theorem on heights, height zero characters, the Fong–Reynolds correspondence and Reynolds' theorem on blocks with a normal defect group, with the height zero and Alperin–McKay conjectures stated as properties of blocks.

ModularCurvesPartII.title: Modular curves, Part II — uniformization, integral boundary and Hecke cohomology
ModularCurvesPartII.description: Compares arithmetic modular curves with analytic quotients of the upper half-plane, builds their integral compactifications and bad fibres, and constructs the Hecke action on their Jacobians and cohomology. Results include compact uniformisation with the fields of definition of the cusps, Ihara's theorems, and the abelian varieties attached to newforms of weight 2 as quotients of modular Jacobians.

ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions.title: Modularity and Langlands extensions
ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions.description: Extends modularity results to Artin representations, potential automorphy, symmetric power functoriality and the Sato–Tate conjecture, and treats packets for classical groups. It sets up the comparisons of normalizations these results need and states the remaining Langlands conjectures precisely.

ModularityAndLanglandsExtensionsPartII.title: Modularity and Langlands extensions, part II — the proof of symmetric power functoriality
ModularityAndLanglandsExtensionsPartII.description: Carries out the proof of symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic modular forms: analytic continuation along eigenvarieties, level raising on unitary groups, automorphy lifting for symmetric powers, and functoriality for tensor products. The final results are the existence of every symmetric power lift of a non-CM newform and the holomorphy of the corresponding symmetric power L-functions.

MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.title: The Mordell conjecture after Lawrence and Venkatesh
MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.description: Proves Faltings's theorem, that a curve of genus at least two over a number field has finitely many rational points, by the method of Lawrence and Venkatesh, and the finiteness of solutions of the S-unit equation by the same method. Along the way it builds p-adic period maps for families of abelian varieties, the Kodaira–Parshin family, and the surface topology and mapping class groups used to show that its monodromy is large.

MordellLawrenceVenkateshPartII.title: The Mordell conjecture after Lawrence and Venkatesh, part II
MordellLawrenceVenkateshPartII.description: Develops the higher-dimensional form of the Lawrence–Venkatesh method, which bounds integral points of a family through p-adic period maps and the Galois representations of its fibres. Its applications are the non-density of integral points in families of projective hypersurfaces and the finiteness, up to translation, of smooth ample hypersurfaces with good reduction in an abelian variety.

NashBlowups.title: Nash blowups
NashBlowups.description: Constructs the Nash blowup of a variety as the closure of the smooth locus in the Grassmannian of rank-d quotients of the sheaf of differentials, together with the normalized Nash blowup and the iterations of both. It proves the universal property, Nobile's theorem that in characteristic zero the Nash blowup is an isomorphism only for smooth varieties, the theorem of Duarte and Núñez-Betancourt for normal varieties in characteristic p, and a principle by which iterated Nash blowups never resolve certain singularities.

NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties.title: Néron models and semistable abelian varieties
NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties.description: Builds Néron models of abelian varieties over discrete valuation rings and Dedekind schemes, their special fibres and component groups, and semistable reduction, including the semistable reduction theorem and the uniformisation of degenerating abelian varieties. Consequences include the criterion of Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, the monodromy pairing, and conductors and local Euler factors.

OperatorTheory/SelfAdjointSpectralTheory.title: Self-adjoint spectral theory: the Borel functional calculus, unbounded operators, and Stone's theorem
OperatorTheory/SelfAdjointSpectralTheory.description: Develops the spectral theory of self-adjoint operators on Hilbert space: one-parameter unitary groups and Stone's theorem, the bounded Borel functional calculus and projection-valued measures, closed operators and their resolvents. Its last part constructs the spectral measure of an unbounded self-adjoint operator through the Cayley transform and states the spectral theorem in that form.

OperatorTheory/UnboundedOperators.title: Unbounded operators on Hilbert space
OperatorTheory/UnboundedOperators.description: Develops closed, densely defined operators on Hilbert space: the unbounded Borel functional calculus, normal operators and joint spectral theory, the essential spectrum, and the decomposition of a self-adjoint operator into pure point, absolutely continuous and singular continuous parts. It also covers symmetric operators and their self-adjoint extensions, closed forms and the Friedrichs extension, analytic vectors, and perturbation theorems of Kato–Rellich type.

PDE.title: Partial differential equations
PDE.description: Develops second-order elliptic and parabolic equations on domains of ℝⁿ: Sobolev and Hölder spaces with their embeddings, traces and compactness, the harmonic-analysis estimates, maximum principles and potential theory. Main results are existence, Fredholm theory and the spectrum for the Dirichlet problem, elliptic regularity (De Giorgi–Nash–Moser, Schauder and Calderón–Zygmund estimates), and parabolic theory with the heat semigroup.

PELModuli.title: Siegel and PEL moduli problems
PELModuli.description: Builds the moduli problems of abelian schemes with a polarization, an action of an order and a level structure, which include the Siegel, Hilbert and unitary cases. It starts from the linear algebra of lattices with an order action and their similitude groups, proves that the moduli problem is a smooth algebraic stack over the appropriate base, and identifies its complex points with a union of arithmetic quotients of hermitian symmetric domains.

PerfectoidSpaces.title: Perfectoid rings and spaces
PerfectoidSpaces.description: Builds perfectoid rings and perfectoid spaces in general, without a perfectoid base field: almost mathematics, tilting, the tilting equivalence with its identification of étale sites, the almost purity theorem and the pro-étale site. It also introduces δ-rings and prisms, which it uses in its treatment of Zariski closed immersions.

PrismaticCohomology.title: Prismatic cohomology, Part I — Delta rings, prisms and relative cohomology
PrismaticCohomology.description: The first part of the prismatic theory: δ-rings and prisms over general rings, the site of bounded prisms, and the relative prismatic cohomology of a formal scheme over a bounded prism. It proves the Hodge–Tate, crystalline and de Rham comparisons for smooth formal schemes and constructs perfectoidizations.

PrismaticCohomologyPartII.title: Prismatic cohomology, Part II — Nygaard filtration, absolute prisms and q-de Rham theory
PrismaticCohomologyPartII.description: The second part of the prismatic theory. It treats Breuil–Kisin twists and the Nygaard filtration, absolute prismatic cohomology through the Cartier–Witt stack, and the q-crystalline and q-de Rham comparisons.

PrismaticCohomologyPartIII.title: Prismatic cohomology, Part III — Étale and syntomic comparisons and F-crystals
PrismaticCohomologyPartIII.description: The third part of the prismatic theory. It proves the étale comparison, builds syntomic complexes, and establishes the equivalence between prismatic F-crystals over a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic and lattices in crystalline Galois representations.

PseudodifferentialOperators.title: Pseudodifferential operators and elliptic analysis on bundles
PseudodifferentialOperators.description: Builds differential operators on vector bundles and the classical pseudodifferential calculus: symbols, quantization, composition and adjoints. On this it develops mapping properties on Sobolev, L^{p}, Hölder and Zygmund spaces, elliptic parametrices with regularity and Fredholm theory on compact manifolds, powers of elliptic operators, and wave front sets.

PseudoholomorphicCurveAnalysis.title: Elliptic analysis of pseudoholomorphic curves
PseudoholomorphicCurveAnalysis.description: Builds the elliptic regularity theory of the Cauchy–Riemann equation used in symplectic topology: Sobolev maps from Riemann surfaces into almost complex manifolds, totally real boundary conditions, and linear estimates for real Cauchy–Riemann operators with Sobolev coefficients. Main results are the elliptic bootstrapping theorem for pseudoholomorphic maps and the Fredholm theory and Riemann–Roch theorem for real Cauchy–Riemann operators on compact surfaces with boundary.

PurityForFlatCohomology.title: Purity for flat cohomology and the conjectures of Gabber
PurityForFlatCohomology.description: Proves purity for flat cohomology after Česnavičius and Scholze: for a Noetherian local complete intersection and a commutative finite flat group scheme, the fppf cohomology with supports in the closed point vanishes below the dimension. It builds fppf cohomology with supports, and deduces purity for torsors and gerbes, Gabber's conjectures on local Picard and Brauer groups, and purity for the Brauer group of regular schemes.

QuantumFoundations.title: Mathematical foundations of quantum systems
QuantumFoundations.description: Sets out the mathematics of quantum systems: states, observables and measurements, projection lattices and Gleason's theorem, dynamics, composite systems and the canonical commutation relations, symmetries and projective representations. It ends with concrete particle models, among them the free Hamiltonian on L²(ℝⁿ), spin, the harmonic oscillator and the hydrogen atom.

QuasiregularMaps.title: Quasiregular maps
QuasiregularMaps.description: Defines quasiregular maps between oriented Riemannian manifolds of the same dimension as continuous Sobolev maps satisfying a distortion inequality, and develops their outer, inner and maximal distortions. Main results are the comparison of these distortions, agreement with the classical definition on Euclidean domains, quasiregularity of suitable simplicial maps, and the first properties of quasiregularly elliptic manifolds, among them that every closed orientable flat manifold is quasiregularly elliptic.

RealSemisimpleLieGroups.title: Real semisimple Lie groups, parabolic subgroups and Riemannian symmetric spaces
RealSemisimpleLieGroups.description: Builds the structure theory of real semisimple and reductive Lie groups on top of the Cartan, Iwasawa and KAK decompositions: Cartan involutions, restricted roots, the real rank, the restricted Weyl group, minimal and general parabolic subgroups with their Langlands decompositions, and the Bruhat decomposition. It then develops the Riemannian symmetric space G/K: its invariant metric, curvature and geodesics, flats and rank, the conjugacy of maximal compact subgroups, and quotients by discrete subgroups.

ReductiveGroupsPartIII.title: Reductive groups, part III — arithmetic conjugacy quotients and tori
ReductiveGroupsPartIII.description: Studies semisimple conjugacy classes and maximal tori of reductive groups over number fields and their completions, starting from the variety of conjugacy classes. Results include the group form of Chevalley's restriction theorem, approximation of local maximal tori by a global one, and the group-theoretic part of the independence of ℓ of Frobenius classes in the Mumford–Tate group of an abelian variety.

RefinedTraceMethods.title: Refined trace methods
RefinedTraceMethods.description: Builds cyclic and cyclotomic refinements of Hochschild homology, the cyclotomic trace from K-theory, and the arithmetic filtrations on topological Hochschild homology and its variants. Its comparisons identify these filtrations with prismatic and syntomic cohomology and with q-Hodge complexes.

RepresentationTheory/LieGroups.title: Lie groups and the Lie algebra correspondence
RepresentationTheory/LieGroups.description: Builds the correspondence between Lie groups and Lie algebras: the exponential map, the adjoint representation, the closed-subgroup theorem, the Lie functor and Lie's third theorem. It continues with the structure of compact and reductive groups: maximal tori and the Weyl integration formula, complexification and real forms, the Borel–Weil theorem, and the Cartan, Iwasawa and KAK decompositions with restricted roots.

RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight.title: Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas
RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight.description: Covers the highest weight theory of semisimple Lie algebras: the enveloping algebra and Verma modules, the Weyl character, dimension and Kostant formulas, the centre of the enveloping algebra with the Harish-Chandra isomorphism, explicit models of the exceptional Lie algebras, and the extension to reductive Lie algebras such as gl(n).

RepresentationTheory/ModularCharactersAn.title: Modular characters and blocks of finite groups
RepresentationTheory/ModularCharactersAn.description: Develops the modular representation theory of a finite group at a prime p: p-modular systems, Brauer characters and the decomposition map, projective characters and Brauer reciprocity, blocks over the three coefficient rings, the Brauer homomorphism and defect groups. Its main results are Brauer's three main theorems, the conjugacy of defect groups, and the behaviour of blocks under normal subgroups.

RiemannianGeometry.title: Curvature, Jacobi fields, submanifolds, and Bochner geometry
RiemannianGeometry.description: Develops Riemannian geometry from curvature onwards: Jacobi fields and index forms, comparison theorems and space forms, isometric immersions with the first and second variation of volume, focal points, and Bochner–Weitzenböck formulas. It also treats Schrödinger-type operators on compact manifolds, and has sub-roadmaps on surfaces and on minimal surfaces.

RiemannianGeometry/MinimalSurfaces.title: Minimal surfaces
RiemannianGeometry/MinimalSurfaces.description: Develops the theory of smooth minimal hypersurfaces in Riemannian manifolds and of minimal surfaces in three-manifolds. Main results include the half-space theorem, ε-regularity and local compactness, the Morse index and stability, the curvature estimate for stable surfaces, removable singularities, Frankel's theorem and the Choi–Schoen compactness theorem.

RiemannianManifoldsWithConvexBoundary.title: Riemannian manifolds with convex boundary
RiemannianManifoldsWithConvexBoundary.description: Treats the boundary of a Riemannian manifold with boundary as a hypersurface: boundary defining functions, the second fundamental form, and strictly convex, convex and strictly concave boundaries with their characterisation by Hessians. It goes on to geodesics at the boundary, boundary normal coordinates, and the exit time and scattering relation of compact non-trapping manifolds.

SchattenClassesAndSchurMultipliers.title: Schatten classes and Schur multipliers
SchattenClassesAndSchurMultipliers.description: Builds Schur multipliers on the Schatten classes of L²(Ω, μ) for a σ-finite measure space, from the kernels of Hilbert–Schmidt operators, with their norms and completely bounded norms. Main results include the Grothendieck–Haagerup characterisation, the theorem of Lafforgue and de la Salle that the norm and the completely bounded norm agree on atomless spaces, transference between Fourier and Schur multipliers on ℝⁿ, and the Hörmander–Mikhlin–Schur multiplier theorem.

SchemeAndStackFoundations.title: Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations
SchemeAndStackFoundations.description: Collects the general algebraic geometry on which the arithmetic roadmaps rest. It covers descent, algebraic spaces, torsors and algebraic stacks; cohomology on the Zariski, étale, fppf and pro-étale sites with coherent duality; curves, divisors and Picard functors; deformation theory, formal schemes and alterations; and Chow groups with Chern classes and Riemann–Roch.

SchrodingerOperatorsAndSpectralTypes.title: Schrödinger operators and spectral types
SchrodingerOperatorsAndSpectralTypes.description: Defines the absolutely continuous, singular continuous and pure point spectra of a self-adjoint operator and proves criteria for them, including the Kato–Rosenblum theorem on trace-class perturbations. It constructs the self-adjoint Laplace–Beltrami operator of a complete Riemannian manifold (the theorem of Gaffney, Chernoff and Strichartz) with its basic spectral properties, and the Schrödinger operators −Δ + V with bounded real potential on L²(ℝ^{d}), with their self-adjointness, cores and essential spectrum.

SeibergWittenTheory.title: Four-dimensional Seiberg–Witten theory
SeibergWittenTheory.description: Constructs Seiberg–Witten theory on a closed oriented smooth four-manifold: the monopole equations for a Spin^{c} structure, the gauge quotient, compactness, transversality and orientations. It defines the Seiberg–Witten invariant and proves its invariance within chambers and its wall-crossing behaviour.

SelmerIwasawaCohomology.title: Selmer groups and Iwasawa cohomology
SelmerIwasawaCohomology.description: Builds Selmer groups and Selmer complexes for p-adic Galois representations, compares local conditions under Tate duality, and carries them up cyclotomic towers and towers with group ℤ_{p}^{d} as Iwasawa cohomology, with control and duality theorems. It includes Kummer theory, Selmer groups and the Tate–Shafarevich group of abelian varieties over number fields, structure theorems for ordinary Selmer groups, and a precise statement of the Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture.

ShimuraData.title: Shimura data, Hermitian domains, and adelic level structures
ShimuraData.description: Builds the Hodge-theoretic and group-theoretic material used with Shimura data: rational weights, Mumford–Tate groups and Hodge-generic abelian varieties, variations of Hodge structure and their polarizations, compact duals over reflex fields, and explicit Hilbert and Siegel data. Its main results are that every connected Shimura datum lifts to a full datum satisfying the additional axioms, and a neatness criterion for certain adelic level subgroups.

ShimuraVarieties.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models
ShimuraVarieties.description: Constructs complex Shimura varieties as towers of arithmetic quotients of hermitian symmetric domains, their Baily–Borel compactifications, and canonical models over reflex fields: first the Siegel case by complex multiplication, then Hodge and abelian type, then general Shimura data. It also treats Mumford–Tate groups and the Galois representations of abelian varieties with values in them.

SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.title: Smooth representations of local groups
SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.description: Builds the smooth representation theory of locally profinite groups over a general coefficient ring, and of reductive p-adic groups in particular: Hecke algebras, parabolic induction and Jacquet functors, admissibility, second adjointness, the Bernstein decomposition and centre, and the Satake isomorphism. These are the local representations and Hecke algebras that the global automorphic theory uses.

SobolevMapsBetweenManifolds.title: Sobolev maps between manifolds
SobolevMapsBetweenManifolds.description: Develops first-order Sobolev maps between manifolds: the class W^{1,p}_{loc}(M, N) of continuous maps with Sobolev chart representatives, the weak differential, its norm and, for oriented Riemannian manifolds of equal dimension, the Jacobian. Main results are independence of charts and metrics, chain rules, pullback of differential forms commuting with the exterior derivative, smooth approximation, and a degree for W^{1,n} maps.

SpectralSequencesAndConvergence.title: Spectral sequences and convergence
SpectralSequencesAndConvergence.description: Builds, over an arbitrary abelian category, the language in which a spectral sequence converges: cycle and boundary towers, the limit page, and weak, ordinary and strong convergence to filtered objects in a prescribed set of degrees. It proves the comparison theorem, convergence for filtered complexes and exact couples under the usual boundedness hypotheses, and Boardman's theorems on conditional convergence.

SpectralSequencesAndConvergencePartII.title: Spectral sequences and convergence, part II — the standard constructions and their products
SpectralSequencesAndConvergencePartII.description: Constructs the standard spectral sequences of homological algebra and proves that they converge: the two spectral sequences of a double complex, the hypercohomology and composite-functor spectral sequences, the universal-coefficient, Künneth and change-of-rings spectral sequences, and the Bockstein spectral sequence. It also treats products, with the Leibniz rule on every page.

StableReduction.title: Stable reduction of curves and stable maps
StableReduction.description: Proves stable reduction for curves over a discrete valuation ring: after a finite extension of the base, a stable model exists and is unique. It also defines stable maps to a scheme and their families, with the stability criteria and the stabilization construction needed for a later proof that the moduli space of stable maps is proper; the moduli stack itself is not constructed here.

StackPointsAndResidualGerbes.title: Points of algebraic stacks, stabilisers and residual gerbes
StackPointsAndResidualGerbes.description: Develops the local structure of an algebraic stack at a point, following the Stacks Project: substacks, finite type and closed points, automorphism groups, gerbes, and the residual gerbe at a point with its existence theorems. Its main results identify the residual gerbe at a rational point with the classifying stack of the automorphism group, and relate the tangent space to the normal space at a closed point.

SurfaceGroupCharacterVarieties.title: Surface group character varieties
SurfaceGroupCharacterVarieties.description: Constructs the outer action of the mapping class group of a punctured surface on its fundamental group, the representation scheme of a finitely generated group, and the character variety of such a group in a real reductive group, the space of reductive representations modulo conjugation. Main results: the character variety is Hausdorff, locally compact and second countable; for complex groups it is homeomorphic to the complex points of the affine quotient; and the mapping class group acts on it by homeomorphisms.

SymplecticGeometry/CotangentLagrangian.title: Cotangent bundles and Lagrangian geometry
SymplecticGeometry/CotangentLagrangian.description: Develops the symplectic geometry of cotangent bundles and Lagrangian submanifolds: the cotangent bundle as a phase space, embedded Lagrangians, generating functions and the canonical transformations they define, and neighbourhood theorems for symplectic germs along a submanifold. Convex planar billiards appear as an example of a map given by a generating function.

TaubesGromov.title: Taubes–Gromov theory
TaubesGromov.description: Constructs Taubes's integer count of embedded pseudoholomorphic curves in a closed symplectic four-manifold and relates it to the Seiberg–Witten invariant through vortices and the monopole equations with a large parameter. It includes the normal operators of embedded curves and an application to mapping tori of surfaces.

TeichmullerGeometry.title: Teichmüller geometry of closed surfaces
TeichmullerGeometry.description: Builds the Teichmüller theory of a closed oriented surface of genus at least two: the space of marked complex structures with its complex structure of dimension 3g − 3, the action of the mapping class group and the Dehn–Nielsen–Baer theorem, Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates, the Teichmüller metric, and the Nielsen realization theorem.

Varifolds.title: Varifolds
Varifolds.description: Builds the theory of k-dimensional varifolds on open subsets of a Riemannian manifold, in the generality of Allard: Radon measures on the Grassmann bundle, their first variation, and stationary, rectifiable and integral varifolds. Main results are the monotonicity formula, Allard's rectifiability theorem, the compactness theorems for rectifiable and integral varifolds, tangent cones and the constancy theorem.

VirtualFundamentalClass.title: The Behrend–Fantechi virtual fundamental class
VirtualFundamentalClass.description: Carries out the construction of Behrend and Fantechi: the intrinsic normal cone of a Deligne–Mumford stack, obstruction theories, and the virtual fundamental class of a perfect obstruction theory with a global resolution, shown to be independent of all choices. Along the way it builds rational Chow groups, Gysin maps and degrees of zero-cycles for separated Deligne–Mumford stacks, and a relative version of the class.

VirtualFundamentalClassPartII.title: Virtual fundamental classes, part II: integral and non-separated Chow theory of Deligne–Mumford stacks and virtual classes over general bases
VirtualFundamentalClassPartII.description: Extends the Chow theory of Deligne–Mumford stacks to integral coefficients and to stacks that need not be separated, with the intersection ring of a smooth stack, the comparison with the moduli space, and the degree of the residual gerbe at a closed point. It defines the virtual class without the resolution property, proves deformation invariance of virtual counts, and constructs the perfect obstruction theory of spaces of maps from curves.

WeilConjectures.title: Weil conjectures and cohomological zeta functions
WeilConjectures.description: Relates point counts over finite fields to the zeta function and its cohomological factors, and assembles the Weil conjectures for a smooth proper scheme over a finite field: integral factors independent of ℓ, the absolute values of the reciprocal roots, and the functional equation. It also contains explicit calculations for curves and surfaces, among them the definition and numerical invariants of Enriques surfaces.

YangMillsConnectionsAndCaloricGauge.title: Yang–Mills connections on Euclidean space and the caloric gauge
YangMillsConnectionsAndCaloricGauge.description: Develops connections on Euclidean space with values in a compact Lie group at critical regularity: Sobolev gauge transformations, Uhlenbeck's Coulomb gauge, the good global gauge theorem, and the topological class and instanton number of a finite-energy connection. It then treats harmonic Yang–Mills connections on ℝ⁴ (energy gap and ground state), the Yang–Mills heat flow, and the caloric gauge of Oh and Tataru, ending with the theorem that the caloric connections form a C¹ submanifold of a Banach space.

definitions.name: Real rank of a semisimple Lie group
definitions.what: The real rank of a real semisimple Lie algebra is the dimension of a maximal abelian subspace of the −1 eigenspace of a Cartan involution, which does not depend on the choices; the real rank of a Lie group with semisimple Lie algebra is that of its Lie algebra.
definitions.first: RealSemisimpleLieGroups states the definition, for Lie algebras and for groups. RepresentationTheory/LieGroups holds the Cartan and Iwasawa decompositions it rests on, and LieGroupsPartII extends the conjugacy of maximal abelian subspaces to groups that need not be connected or semisimple.
definitions.library: Tau Ceti has the Cartan decomposition G = K·exp(𝔭) of the general and special linear groups over ℝ and ℂ and of the real symplectic group, and the Iwasawa decomposition G = KAN of the general linear group over ℝ and ℂ and of SL(n, ℝ). It has no Cartan involution of a general real semisimple Lie algebra, no restricted roots and no real rank.

definitions.name: p-block (Brauer block) of a finite group
definitions.what: A p-block of a finite group G is a primitive idempotent of the centre of the group algebra of G over a complete discrete valuation ring whose residue field has characteristic p (equivalently, over that residue field); each irreducible character of G belongs to exactly one block.

definitions.name: Defect group of a block
definitions.what: A defect group of a block b of a finite group G is a subgroup D that is minimal with the property that b is a relative trace from the D-fixed points of the group algebra under conjugation; defect groups are p-subgroups and form a single conjugacy class.
definitions.first: RepresentationTheory/ModularCharactersAndBlocks states the definition; ModularCharactersAndBlocksPartII proves further theorems about defect groups.

definitions.name: Parabolic subgroups of a real semisimple Lie group (minimal and standard parabolics)
definitions.what: In a connected real semisimple Lie group G with finite centre and Iwasawa decomposition G = KAN, the minimal parabolic subgroup is P = MAN with M the centraliser of A in K; the standard parabolic subgroups are the subgroups containing P, indexed by the sets of simple restricted roots, and a parabolic subgroup is a conjugate of one of them; each has a Langlands decomposition.
definitions.first: RealSemisimpleLieGroups states the whole definition, for connected groups with semisimple Lie algebra and finite centre. The minimal parabolic subgroup alone is also stated in AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups, for the real points of reductive groups, and in LieGroupsPartII, for reductive groups that need not be connected.
definitions.library: Tau Ceti has parabolic subgroups of an affine algebraic group over a field, defined as the smooth closed subgroups that contain a Borel subgroup over an algebraic closure; the subgroup attached to a cocharacter of an affine group scheme, with its Levi decomposition on points; and the standard parabolic subgroups of a group with a Tits system. It has no parabolic subgroups defined from the Iwasawa decomposition and the restricted roots of a real semisimple Lie group, and no Langlands decomposition.

definitions.name: Infinitesimal character (and Casimir eigenvalue) of a representation of a real reductive group
definitions.what: A module over the enveloping algebra of the complexified Lie algebra of a real reductive group has an infinitesimal character if the centre of the enveloping algebra acts on it by scalars; by the Harish-Chandra isomorphism the resulting character of the centre is a Weyl group orbit of linear forms on a Cartan subalgebra, and the scalar by which the Casimir element acts is the Casimir eigenvalue.

It also has the Casimir element, proved central, with the scalar by which it acts on a highest weight module, and the modules over an algebra on which the centre acts through a given character. The infinitesimal character of a representation of a real reductive group, taken on its smooth vectors, is not there.

definitions.name: Convergence of a spectral sequence
definitions.what: A spectral sequence converges to a family of filtered objects Hⁿ when its limit page is identified with the graded pieces of the filtrations and each filtration is exhaustive and separated; weak convergence drops the two conditions on the filtrations, and strong convergence adds completeness.
definitions.first: SpectralSequencesAndConvergence states the definition; SpectralSequencesAndConvergencePartII constructs the standard spectral sequences and proves that they converge in this sense.
definitions.library: Tau Ceti has, for a spectral object in an abelian category, the abutment with its filtration and the identification of the limit terms with the graded pieces. For the spectral sequence of a filtered complex it proves strong convergence when the filtration is finite and, for complexes of modules, when the filtration is exhaustive, or complete and exhaustive, under a boundedness condition in each degree. Convergence, weak or strong, is not defined as a notion for an arbitrary spectral sequence.

definitions.name: Spin^{c} structure on an oriented manifold
definitions.what: A Spin^{c} structure on an oriented Riemannian n-manifold is a principal Spin^{c}(n)-bundle with an equivariant map to the bundle of oriented orthonormal frames, where Spin^{c}(n) is the quotient of Spin(n) × U(1) by the element (−1, −1).
definitions.first: FourManifolds states it in every rank; HeegaardFloer gives the vector-field description on three-manifolds; SeibergWittenTheory builds on FourManifolds.

It does not define a Spin^{c} structure as a principal Spin^{c}(n)-bundle over the frame bundle.

definitions.name: Strict stability of a minimal cone/hypersurface (Simon's inequality)
definitions.what: A minimal hypersurface is stable when the quadratic form ∫(|∇ζ|² − |A|²ζ²) is nonnegative on test functions; it is strictly stable, in the sense of Simon, when this form is bounded below by a positive multiple of ∫(|∇ζ|² + r^{−2}ζ²) for a fixed positive weight r, the hypersurface being allowed a singular set.
definitions.caveat: Not found: strict stability is not specified in any roadmap. RiemannianGeometry has the second variation form and ordinary stability of smooth minimal hypersurfaces.
definitions.first: No roadmap states strict stability. For ordinary stability look first at RiemannianGeometry, section R5b.

definitions.name: Strictly convex boundary of a Riemannian manifold
definitions.what: The boundary of a Riemannian manifold with boundary is strictly convex at a point when its second fundamental form there is positive definite, and strictly convex when this holds at every boundary point.

definitions.name: Local components of an automorphic representation (restricted tensor product)
definitions.what: The local component at a place v of an irreducible admissible automorphic representation π of a reductive group over a number field is the irreducible representation π_{v} of the local group, unique up to isomorphism, for which π is the restricted tensor product of the π_{v}, formed with respect to spherical vectors at almost all places.
definitions.first: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups states the restricted tensor product and the factorisation into local components; AutomorphicSpectralTheory and AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors apply it.

definitions.name: Arithmetic lattice in a semisimple Lie group
definitions.what: A lattice in a semisimple real Lie group G is arithmetic if it is commensurable with the image of the integer points of a connected semisimple algebraic group H over ℚ under a continuous surjection with compact kernel from the identity component of H(ℝ) onto G.

definitions.library: Mathlib has the notion only for subgroups of GL₂(ℝ): those commensurable with the image of SL₂(ℤ). Tau Ceti does not define arithmetic lattices in a general semisimple Lie group.

definitions.name: Galois representation attached to a cuspidal Hecke eigenform
definitions.what: For an eigenform f of weight k ≥ 2, level N and character ε, and a place λ of its coefficient field above a prime ℓ, this is the continuous two-dimensional λ-adic representation of the absolute Galois group of ℚ, unique up to isomorphism, that is unramified outside Nℓ and in which Frobenius at a prime p not dividing Nℓ has characteristic polynomial X² − a_{p}X + ε(p)p^{k−1}, where a_{p} is the eigenvalue of the Hecke operator at p.

definitions.name: Abelian scheme with complex multiplication by O_{L} of CM type Σ
definitions.what: For a number field L of degree 2d containing a CM field, this is an abelian scheme of relative dimension d with an action of the ring of integers of L whose Lie algebra, decomposed according to the embeddings of L, has rank one at the embeddings in a given CM type Σ of L and vanishes at the others.

definitions.what: A cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂ over a number field has complex multiplication if it is isomorphic to its twist by some nontrivial Hecke character.

definitions.what: For an abelian scheme with complex multiplication by the integers of L of type Σ, defined over a subring of ℂ and equipped with bases of invariant differentials on it and on its dual and with an identification of its first homology with the integers of L, the complex periods are the two families of complex numbers, indexed by Σ and by the conjugate type, obtained by integrating the chosen differentials over the chosen generator of homology.

definitions.name: Critical infinity types Crit_{L}(Γ) and the attached CM type
definitions.what: For a number field L containing a CM field and a subgroup Γ of finite index in its units, a critical infinity type is an integer-valued function μ on the embeddings of L of the form taken by infinity types of algebraic Hecke characters, with ε^{μ} = 1 for every unit ε in Γ, whose negative values occur exactly on a CM type of L; that CM type is the one attached to μ.

definitions.name: Emerton's completed cohomology of modular curves
definitions.what: For a fixed level away from p, the completed cohomology of modular curves is the inverse limit over n of the direct limit, over levels at p shrinking to the identity, of the cohomology of the modular curves with coefficients in ℤ/pⁿ; it carries commuting actions of GL₂(ℚ_{p}), of the Galois group of ℚ and of the Hecke operators away from p.

definitions.name: Good reduction of a hypersurface in an abelian variety
definitions.what: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field with good reduction at a finite place v; a hypersurface H in A has good reduction at v if its closure in the abelian scheme extending A over the local ring at v is smooth over that ring.

definitions.name: Minimal parabolic subgroups and the Langlands decomposition (real rank one)
definitions.what: A minimal parabolic subgroup of a connected semisimple Lie group G with finite centre is P = MAN, where G = KAN is an Iwasawa decomposition and M is the centraliser of A in K; the factorisation P = MAN is its Langlands decomposition.

definitions.library: Tau Ceti has the Iwasawa decomposition G = KAN of the general linear group over ℝ and ℂ and of SL(n, ℝ), and parabolic subgroups of affine algebraic groups over a field. It has no Iwasawa decomposition of a general semisimple Lie group, and no minimal parabolic subgroup or Langlands decomposition built from one.

definitions.what: For a geometrically connected variety X over a number field K, a class of sections of the map from the étale fundamental group of X to the absolute Galois group of K is Selmer if at every place its restriction comes from a local point; at a finite place where local points inject into local sections, the localisation map sends a Selmer section to that local point.

definitions.name: Symmetric power of a Weil–Deligne representation

definitions.name: Tate–Shafarevich group of an abelian variety over a number field
definitions.what: The Tate–Shafarevich group of an abelian variety A over a number field K is the subgroup of the Galois cohomology group H¹(K, A) consisting of the classes that become trivial in H¹(K_{v}, A) at every place v.
definitions.first: SelmerIwasawaCohomology, section 2.12a, defines it together with the Selmer groups of an isogeny; EllipticCurves specifies the elliptic-curve case; NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties compares it with torsors under the connected Néron model, and HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions uses it for descent.
definitions.library: Tau Ceti has the Tate–Shafarevich group of an elliptic curve in Weierstrass form over a number field, the classes in H¹(K, E) that vanish over every completion, together with its Selmer groups. Mathlib defines a Tate–Shafarevich group for the continuous cohomology of a Galois module and a family of extensions of the base field. Neither is applied to an abelian variety of dimension greater than one.

definitions.name: Weak functorial transfer to GL_{N}
definitions.what: Given a reductive group G over a number field and a representation r of its L-group into GL_{N}, an automorphic representation Π of GL_{N} is a weak functorial transfer of an automorphic representation π of G if at almost all unramified places the Satake parameter of Π is the image under r of that of π, and at each archimedean place the infinitesimal characters correspond under r.
definitions.caveat: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartII states it for split symplectic, special orthogonal and general spin groups with the standard representation of the dual group; the general definition, for an arbitrary representation of the L-group, was not found in any roadmap.

definitions.name: ℓ-adic Galois representation with values in the Mumford–Tate group
definitions.what: For an abelian variety A over a number field whose ℓ-adic Galois representation on H¹ takes values in the ℚ_{ℓ}-points of the Mumford–Tate group G of A, one obtains a continuous homomorphism from the Galois group to G(ℚ_{ℓ}); at a place of good reduction the image of Frobenius gives a point of the variety of semisimple conjugacy classes of G.

definitions.name: The π-nearly isotypic cuspidal subspace
definitions.what: For an irreducible admissible representation π of the adelic points of a reductive group, the π-nearly isotypic subspace of the cuspidal L² space is the closure of the sum of the irreducible cuspidal subrepresentations whose local components are isomorphic to those of π at almost all places.

definitions.name: Anosov flow
definitions.what: A C¹ flow on a compact Riemannian manifold, generated by a vector field X without zeros, is Anosov if the tangent bundle splits invariantly as E^{s} ⊕ ℝX ⊕ E^{u}, with the flow contracting E^{s} and expanding E^{u} at uniform exponential rates.

definitions.name: Billiard ball map of a convex billiard table
definitions.what: For a strictly convex planar table whose boundary is parametrised by arclength, the billiard ball map sends a boundary point and an outgoing angle to the next point where the straight trajectory meets the boundary and the angle after reflection there; it is a map of the phase cylinder (ℝ/ℓℤ) × (0, π).
definitions.first: MathematicalBilliards states the definition, for tables of class C^{k}; CotangentLagrangian has the map for smooth tables, and MathematicalBilliards section 2.5 identifies the two.
definitions.library: Tau Ceti has the billiard map of a table whose boundary is parametrised by arclength and satisfies a strict convexity condition on its tangent lines: the next-collision map, the induced bijection of the phase cylinder in the coordinates (s, cos δ), its inverse by time reversal, and the chord-length generating function with the twist condition. Continuity of the map is not proved, the table is not obtained from a curve of positive curvature, and rotational invariant curves are not there.

definitions.what: The billiard flow of a polygon moves a point with a unit velocity vector along straight lines at unit speed, reflecting the velocity in a side at each collision; it acts on the phase space of unit vectors with the boundary identifications, away from the trajectories that reach a vertex, and preserves the Liouville measure.

definitions.name: Borel complete class of countable structures
definitions.what: An isomorphism-invariant Borel class K of countable structures is Borel complete if, for every such class in any countable language, its isomorphism relation is Borel reducible to the isomorphism relation of K.

definitions.name: Dynamical degree of a dominant rational self-map
definitions.what: For a dominant rational self-map f of a projective variety of dimension d and 0 ≤ k ≤ d, the k-th dynamical degree is the limit of the n-th roots of the k-th degrees of the iterates fⁿ, where the k-th degree is an intersection number on the graph of the map taken with respect to an ample class.

definitions.name: Equilibrium state (measure) of a Hölder potential
definitions.what: For a continuous map or flow on a compact metric space and a continuous potential φ, an equilibrium state is an invariant probability measure for which the entropy plus the integral of φ equals the topological pressure of φ, the supremum of this quantity over all invariant probability measures.
definitions.first: ClassicalErgodicTheory states the definition, with pressure and the variational principle; HyperbolicDynamicsAndThermodynamicFormalism proves existence and uniqueness for Hölder potentials on hyperbolic systems.

definitions.what: A measure of maximal entropy of a continuous map of a compact metric space is an invariant Borel probability measure whose Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy equals the topological entropy of the map.

definitions.name: Polish space of countable structures Mod_{L}(ω)
definitions.what: For a countable language L, the space of L-structures with universe ℕ is the product of the spaces of interpretations of the symbols of L; it is a Polish space on which the group of permutations of ℕ acts by relabelling, and the orbits are the isomorphism classes.
definitions.first: CountableStructureSpaces states the definition for relational languages; CountableStructureSpacesPartII adds function symbols.
definitions.library: Tau Ceti has, for the relation symbols of a language, the space of structures on ℕ with its product topology, which is Polish when the language is countable; the permutation group of ℕ as a Polish group; its action on structures by relabelling; and isomorphism as the orbit relation of this action. Function symbols are not interpreted in this space.

definitions.name: Scaling limit of lattice φ^{4} fields (reachable random field)
definitions.what: A random field on ℝ^{d} is reachable if its finite-dimensional distributions are limits of those of rescaled lattice fields, smeared against test functions, under finite-volume φ⁴ or Ising measures, as the volume and then the scale tend to infinity.

definitions.name: Translation-invariant ergodic Gibbs measure on lozenge tilings of given slope
definitions.what: A probability measure on the lozenge tilings of the plane is a Gibbs measure if, given the tiling outside any finite region, the tiling inside is uniformly distributed among those compatible with it; the definition singles out the translation-invariant, ergodic Gibbs measure of a given slope (s, t), the pair of densities of two of the three types of lozenge.
definitions.caveat: The roadmap constructs an ergodic Gibbs measure of every slope and describes it by its determinantal kernel; the uniqueness of the measure of a given slope is not part of this roadmap.
